title: Optimistic reconnect probe and JSONL boundary safety for SSE streaming with function-call atomicity
creator: Jordan Lee
description: Implement an optimistic reconnect probe and JSONL/NDJSON boundary safety layer for our SSE streaming API. This ticket focuses on enabling clients to reconnect quickly after transient connection failures without duplicating completed function-call tool invocations or corrupting structured JSONL output. It introduces a small, backwards-compatible probe handshake and a compact sequence stamp that allows partial rehydration of the final output up to the last reliably-acknowledged logical boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Clients can reconnect within 500ms typical and resume stream without replaying already-applied function calls
Structured JSONL output remains well-formed after client-side reassembly and server-side resume up to an accepted checkpoint
Server returns an optimistic probe result when capacity/latency permits; otherwise returns canonical fallback that preserves idempotency
E2E tests cover reconnect with interleaved function-call frames and verify single-application of tool invocations
No change required for existing clients: probe handshake is optional and ignored by older clients
technical_notes:
Design summary:

1) Probe handshake: on TCP/TLS re-establishment the client MAY send a 1-line probe event (X-Resume-Probe: <seq_stamp>) as an SSE comment/initial event. The server responds with a single-line status event indicating accepted_resume|reject|defer and an optional resume_index. This probe is optimistic: if accepted, client will request resume starting from server-provided offset. If rejected, client falls back to full restart.

2) Sequence stamps: compact base64-encoded token containing (stream_id, last_committed_frame_index, short-hash). These are scoped per-session/model-route and short-lived (minutes). They are cryptographically MACed with server key to prevent tampering.

3) Logical boundaries: streaming frames are tagged with logical_boundary:number and boundary_type:{delta|partial|functioncall_start|functioncall_end}. The server guarantees that the last committed logical boundary is idempotent with respect to side-effects (function calls).

4) Function-call atomicity: when a function call is emitted in the stream, the runtime marks it with a durable function_invocation_id. Reconnect accept requires that either the server has recorded invocation_id as applied or it will provide a safe rewind point before functioncall_start. Clients must not re-apply a function call unless their probe indicates no server-side application.

5) JSONL/NDJSON safety: we enforce line-delimited structured outputs for tool payloads. On reconnect, partial last-line fragments are discarded unless the server supplies the full reconstructed line at resume_index. This avoids malformed parse trees in downstream consumers.

6) Backpressure/negotiation: a small header field X-Client-Window tells server preferred max-replay-window. The server can override and communicate reduced window in probe response. This allows a best-effort balance between low reconnection latency and server memory for rehydration.

Trade-offs considered:
- Increased server bookkeeping for short-lived resume windows vs. improved UX and reduced duplicated side-effects. Chosen short TTL for sequence stamps to limit memory and attack surface.
- MACed stamps add key rotation complexity; will integrate with KMS rotation flow already used for other signed tokens.

Compatibility:
- Older clients ignore probe and continue to rely on existing reconnect fallback behavior. New clients can opt in to probe by including X-Resume-Probe comment. Server will not require it.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge feature behind feature flag 'optimistic-resume' for API nodes.
2) Smoke deploy to canary cluster for 48 hours with synthetic reconnect tests.
3) Enable feature for 10% of hosted traffic, monitor replay rate and duplicate-function-call incidents.
4) If stable, expand to 50% then 100%.
5) Coordinate SDK release (js/python) that implements probe+reassembly helpers before enabling default opt-in in Console.
tests: unit: seq_stamp encode/decode, MAC verification and TTL enforcement
integration: client reconnect after chunk boundary with functioncall in-flight, ensure single application
e2e: synthetic load with intermittent network blips, measure reconnect latency and duplicate count
fuzz: malformed partial JSONL fragments during resume, ensure server returns fully-formed lines or instructs drop
comments: 2026-02-11: Initial writeup and architecture proposal posted. Asked infra for requirements on short-lived token storage. - Jordan Lee
2026-02-16: Design review with Security: agreed to MAC stamps with KMS-backed signing, rotate keys weekly. Security requested a threat model doc. - Priya Nair

2026-02-18: Spike complete: prototype probe handshake added to sse-shim. Local tests show average cold-reconnect latency from 1.2s -> 320ms when accepted. Memory footprint for 60s window ~40KB/node under current load. - Samir Khan

2026-02-22: QA ran e2e with function-call replay scenarios. Found bug: duplicate invocation when function_call_end arrives exactly while connection drops. Identified fix: server must ack functioncall_end before marking invocation applied. Patch in review. - Priya Nair
